en: Are you sure? I'll take really good care of it, promise.
Oh. Thanks.
What's this? What am I even supposed to do with it?
What? You're giving me another one of these?
You gave me this before. Do you give out so many you forget who you gave them to, or what?
I hope you'll come see me again, Kiryu-san!
I like you. I'll be sure to ask for you next time.
Really!? I can't wait!
I had lots of fun today!
Haha! <Color:255,200,200,255>⑮<Color:Default>
Thanks for coming today. Stop by again, okay?
See you next time.
I'll see you around! <Color:255,200,200,255>⑮<Color:Default>
Oh, that's super common. But hey, at least it's useful.
Oooh, that's a good one! Lucky you, Kiryu-san!
No, I'm sure I can do better.
Oh wow! I almost never see anyone win those! Better take care of that.
Thanks for the tip.
Whoa, you hit the jackpot! You're really lucky, Kiryu-san! <Color:255,200,200,255>⑮<Color:Default>
One bottle of champagne, please!
Hello there. Welcome to Elise.
You'd like to see Hinata-san? This way, sir.
I'm terribly sorry, sir, but Hinata-san isn't here at the moment, I'm afraid.
(Maybe I should order something.)
(She already said yes. What am I trying to do here?)
(She already turned me down once. I should wait a while before I ask her again.)
This club has a big stage for singing karaoke, but I haven't used it yet.
I guess there is one, huh? I've come to this club a number of times, but I've never seen anybody using it myself.
I'm super into karaoke! I'm really itching to get up there and do it!
I love being up on stage. Just seeing a mic stand gets me all pumped up to sing.
Right!? So I was super happy to see I have a stage where I can sing every day. But for some reason I've just never gotten around to it.
Lately, karaoke pubs are all the rage. This place doesn't have that kind of vibe.
I get stage fright. I can't bring myself to sing in front of a bunch of people I don't know.
What? No! It's really, really fun!
You should just get up and sing your heart out! Once you get going, I guarantee you won't be able to stop!
Easier said than done.

en: Are you taking requests? I can give you one if you want to get up there and sing.
Well, the thing is, the stage is off-limits right now. It's reserved for special events and holidays like Christmas.
Oh, really? Then yeah, I guess you wouldn't have much opportunity to use it.
You should come during an event! I'll keep singing as long as I get requests!
You like karaoke that much?
I love it! If I'm not careful, I'll spend an entire day off singing.
Wait. There's no way you can sing all day long.
Oh yes there is! Get in first thing in the morning when it's free, sing until 7:00 PM, have a quick dinner, and then keep going all night long!
That's amazing. Not only can you have fun for all that time, but you can get people to stay with you for so long, too.
Well, sometimes I have to call in others partway through when they're free.
People drop in and out. If everyone managed to stick around, the room would get so crowded!
The more the merrier. It's fun to pass the mic around and do big group sing-alongs.
Oh, no, I can't do that. It bugs me when someone interrupts me while I sing.
And people who enter in a bunch of songs out of turn drive me up the wall.
I guess we have different tastes.
I prefer smaller groups. If there are too many people, I don't get to sing as much.
Yeah, that's true! If you only get to sing once every hour, you get bored and just wind up messing around on your phone the whole time.
I think four or five people is the ideal number.
That's overdoing it. You'll mess up your throat if you keep singing for that long.
Well, it's not like it's just me singing the entire time. I spend plenty of time listening to other people sing too, so it's fine.
If anything, I think this job here is what's worse for my throat, given the constant talking and drinking liquor.
The air quality here isn't good either. Even if all you're doing is talking, that definitely puts a strain on your throat.
Right! That's why karaoke's better.
And I always get no-smoking rooms for karaoke, too. Any smokers can take it outside.
Yeah, singing in a room that's filled with tobacco smoke can't be good for you.
It's still better than singing. Even one intense song can put a lot of strain on your throat.
That's only bad if you sing from your throat! Do you speak from your throat, Kiryu-san?
Well, of course I do.
No, you don't. Your voice comes from your belly! With proper abdominal breathing, you don't need to risk injuring your throat.
I don't think I could ever put in that much effort just to master my karaoke technique.
You really don't tire of it? I'm usually only good for about two hours.
Well, if it starts to get old, you can just shove the table aside and dance, or even just talk. Other people fall asleep later at night.
At least you're not tone deaf. I think people who are embarrassed by their lack of singing talent have an easier time that way.
Oh, I can't stand listening to tone deaf people sing. I keep smiling and pretend like I'm busy looking for my next song, but it's rough.
Maybe you should be careful not to let other people see that.
If you're just going to be doing whatever you want, it's better to stay home than it is to blow your money on going to karaoke.
Yeah, that's maybe not a bad idea. I can do karaoke at home, after all.
Lots of places have kicked me out for making too much of a racket, so maybe that's what I'll do next time!
Just try not to keep the neighbors up.
Kiryu-san, do you like liver sashimi?
Yeah. Whenever I go out for yakiniku, that's usually what I wind up getting.
Hehe. I love liver sashimi, too.
Oh, really? I hear a lot of women do.
Oh, yes! Whenever I go out for yakiniku with my girlfriends, we always get ourselves a plate apiece.
Wow. Guess you really do like it.
That's unusual. I didn't think most women liked it very much.
What are you talking about? My friends eat it all the time, too.
Huh. I wouldn't have guessed.
I also crave iron like mad when I get anemic.
But it's been tough lately because I haven't been able to eat any.
Guess you'll have to tough it out. We have to wait until our raw meat is deemed safe enough to eat again.
No! I don't care if it's safe or not. I just want to eat it!
Wow, you really do like it. Guess you'll have to look for someplace where it's still available.
Do you know any places, Kiryu-san?
No, it's been a while since I've been back in Tokyo. I'm not really up to date on things.
I see. I'm sure there has to be someplace here in Kamurocho that has it.
Maybe I can keep an eye out for you.
But you might die. Just be grateful that you were able to eat it up until now.
Well, Kiryu-san. Drinking and smoking are bad for you, too, but you wouldn't quit that, right?
Now that you mention it, even though I know full well it's bad for me, I still can't bring myself to stop.
See? So there's nothing wrong with me wanting to have some liver sashimi!
Alright, sure. Go for it.
That's different. Drinking and smoking won't kill you if you don't overdo them, but even one bad piece of liver sashimi can be dangerous.
Are you for real? Way, way, way more people have died because of alcohol and cigarettes than they have from liver sashimi!
Okay, I can't really argue with you there. I guess I'd be fine with it if the place was somewhere that was certified to be safe.
Why not find a substitute? There are similar foods out there you could eat.
Oh yeah, like what?
Let's see. One of my passengers told me about this new konjac jelly that's like liver sashimi.
Konjac jelly!?
Yeah. You eat it with sesame oil, and it apparently has a similar taste and texture.
Wow, that's really a thing? I'll have to try it!
I don't think it's rich in iron, though.
I'm sure you could find some. Lots of places will serve it even if they don't put it on the menu.
Well, that's what I was doing until recently, but that trick's a bust now. Restaurants just won't prepare it anymore.
Really? Wow, then I guess you really can't eat it right now.
Aww. All sorts of foods carry the risk of food poisoning, but nooo! For some reason, liver sashimi gets singled out. It's not fair!
Guess you'll have to hope it gets deemed safe to eat again.
Don't give up. Some places will make it, but not for customers they aren't familiar with.
If they make it but won't serve it to me, then what's the point?
It's just how secret menu stuff works. They'll make things as a special favor for regulars, but not for ordinary customers.
So if you keep going a bunch and then ask, you'll get someplace to serve it to you eventually.
Oh, I get it! So I need to become a regular someplace!
What are you looking at?
Oh, sorry. I was just checking Chatter.
Is that an internet thing?
Yeah. I was just wondering what everyone was up to right now.
Young people are always messing around on their phones nowadays. I always see people at dinner who don't even bother to look up at each other.
Yeah, that's for sure.
That's rude, don't you think? Especially when someone's trying to have a conversation with you.
Oh, I'm sorry.
It's a generation gap thing. Back when I was your age, I don't think we even had cell phones.
Wow, really!? Haha, I can't imagine life without cell phones!
Hmph. Well, I don't understand why you youngsters can't keep your mitts off of them.
Yeah, I'm such an addict! I can't sit for very long before I gotta get out my phone and start fiddling with it.
So it's a time waster? Hm. When I'm bored because I don't have any passengers, I just reread the newspaper over and over.
See? That's the problem! Magazines and stuff are way too easy to breeze through. But the internet always has plenty of new stuff to look at.
Really? I've never gotten the hang of using a cell phone, myself. What the heck do you keep looking at on it anyways?
Hmm. Well, I check people's blogs, social media feeds, and mess around with apps.
But trying to keep up with everything would take way too much time, so I only focus on a small set of things.
You must have a lot of friends. I don't know many people, so I'd be done checking up on them in no time.
Hey, Kiryu-san, you should friend me! Then your screen will be full of all the stuff I post, and you'll never get bored!
I don't think I'm ready for that yet.
You know you don't need to read all of it. It'd be impossible for someone with a lot of friends.
Yeah, I started trying to stick to just friends, but now I follow a lot of strangers, too.
So I made a separate account for my close friends only, and I mostly stick to using that.
I guess young people put a lot of effort into personal relationships, too.
Why not try something else? What's the point of reading nothing but a bunch of silly messages?
Well, that's my business. It's not like I spend all day looking at my phone. I do lots of other things, too.
But you're supposed to be serving customers.
That doesn't get tiresome? I like watching TV because when a show is over, you know you're done with it.
Yeah, but people go to sleep at night, so updates tend to stop altogether by early in the morning.
On the other hand, some people <Italic>only </Italic> update during those times. You figure they must work the night shift.
So I'll tell them things like, "Good luck at work!" and stuff.
I see. So you can always keep up with your friends. That's kind of neat.
Sounds like an addiction all right. You should try to rein in your use, don't you think?
That's easy for you to say, sure. But I bet you couldn't stop smoking either, Kiryu-san.
Maybe not. I can't smoke while I'm driving, so if I have a long shift I get a bit cranky.
See? That's how it goes with me and my phone, too.
I know where you're coming from now. You need to take quick breaks from work to stay focused.
Yeah, exactly. I knew you'd understand!
Just don't do it so much that you wind up getting your customers upset with you for it.
It's not the same. I can abstain when I'm on the clock, but you can't stop checking your phone, even at work.
Aha! You got me there, Kiryu-san!
Are you sure you're okay?
Aren't you on the clock now? You should focus on your customers.
But if I go too long without checking my phone, I lose my ability to concentrate.
